Anyone relying on this claim for Benko's current custodial exposure would be materially wrong — the operative sentence is 30 months, not two years. The evidentiary base is also entirely secondary journalism: no court order or Austrian primary-adjacent source (ORF, APA, Der Standard) has been examined; thelocal.at (2025-10-15) attributes the sentence only to 'an Austrian court,' so the specific Innsbruck Regional Court attribution rests on costar.com and retrospective 2026 pieces; and none of the snippets states whether the two years was imposed in full or partially suspended, which Austrian courts commonly do. That said, honesty requires conceding this is a weak runner-up: the claim is explicitly time-anchored ('in October 2025'), and as a historical assertion it is corroborated by two independent contemporaneous reports dated 15-17 October 2025 plus three retrospective 2026 reports, so the realistic alternatives are TRUE or at most MIXED (if read as stating the current sentence), not FALSE.
would_flip_it: A primary or authoritative record of the October 2025 Innsbruck judgment (court order, APA/ORF/Der Standard report, or official court statement) showing the disposition was not a two-year prison sentence — e.g., acquittal, a different sentence length, a materially different suspended/unconditional split, or a verdict actually delivered in a different month or by a different court.
